title: InvDiff: Invariant Guidance for Bias Mitigation in Diffusion Models

problem.claim: Diffusion models can inherit imbalances and biases from real-world training data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches may rely on known-bias prompts or bias labels, but real-world settings include unknown biases and bias labels are difficult to obtain.

contributions.claim: InvDiff learns invariant semantic information for guidance and uses it to mitigate bias in pre-trained diffusion models without auxiliary bias annotations.
The framework identifies underlying training-data biases, introduces a debiasing training objective, and uses a lightweight trainable module without altering the pre-trained diffusion model.
The authors provide a theoretical guarantee relating InvDiff's implementation to reducing the generalization-error upper bound.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the debiasing training objective as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three publicly available benchmarks are reported to show reduced bias while maintaining image-generation quality.
The authors report that their code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion models are effective generative models that learn high-dimensional data distributions but can inherit real-world data biases.
Prior mitigation approaches face limitations because unknown biases are common and bias labels are difficult to obtain.
InvDiff learns invariant semantic information, identifies underlying biases, and guides sampling with a lightweight module without modifying the pre-trained model.
The paper states a theoretical guarantee connecting InvDiff to a reduced generalization-error upper bound.
Results on three public benchmarks are reported to reduce bias while preserving image-generation quality.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method targets unknown biases without requiring auxiliary bias annotations.

interpretation.claim: Bias mitigation can be framed around learning invariant semantic information rather than depending exclusively on predefined bias labels.

application.claim: For generative systems deployed on data with incomplete bias inventories, consider annotation-light guidance modules that preserve invariant semantics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how well the approach handles particular bias types, domains, or deployment conditions.

unknowns: The specific benchmark datasets, bias categories, baselines, and quantitative results are not stated.
The mechanism for identifying underlying biases and the debiasing objective are not specified.
The assumptions and scope of the theoretical guarantee are not stated.
